record.summary: Requires operators of companion chatbot platforms to disclose that interactions are artificially generated and to keep protocols for detecting and responding to suicidal ideation and self-harm, including crisis referrals. For minors it requires break reminders and blocks sexually explicit images. Operators must report self-harm protocols and crisis-referral statistics to public health authorities, and families have a private right of action against noncompliant and negligent developers.
record.notes: Passed the Assembly 59-1 on 10 Sep 2025 and the Senate 33-3 on 11 Sep 2025; signed on 13 Oct 2025 as Chapter 677, Statutes of 2025, in a package on children's online safety that also included AB 1043 (age verification signals), AB 316 (artificial intelligence: defenses), AB 621 (deepfake pornography) and AB 853 (California AI Transparency Act amendments). Effective 1 Jan 2026. On 10 Sep 2026 the Governor signed SB 1119 ('Companion chatbots: children's safety') and SB 867 ('Toys: companion chatbots'); his release says the 2025 protections for AI companion chatbots were strengthened again that day.

verification.note: Recheck of 18 Oct 2026. Stored and read: the Governor's release of 13 Oct 2025 (gov.ca.gov, copy of 17 Oct 2026), which lists SB 243 (Padilla), 'Companion chatbots', among the bills signed that day and describes its duties; Senator Padilla's release of 13 Oct 2025 (sd18.senate.ca.gov), which gives the signing, the floor votes, the private right of action and 'The bill becomes law on January 1st, 2026'; the Assembly Privacy and Consumer Protection Committee's 2025 bill summary (apcp.assembly.ca.gov), which gives Chapter 677, Statutes of 2025; and the Governor's release of 10 Sep 2026 (gov.ca.gov), which lists SB 1119 and SB 867. The bill's page on leginfo.legislature.ca.gov refused automated downloads (HTTP 403). Version 1's date_last_updated (10 Sep 2026, the signing of SB 1119) was removed: the release of 10 Sep 2026 says the 2025 protections were 'again strengthened', and Senator Padilla's release of 31 Aug 2026 (stored for US-CA-08) says SB 1119 builds on SB 243, but no stored file shows that SB 1119 amends SB 243's sections. Version 1's reporting start of 1 Jul 2027 rests on no source and was removed from the notes.

summary.locator: release, list 'The bills will help protect children online by creating'
summary.quote: New safeguards on AI chatbots by establishing requirements that “companion chatbot” platforms create protocols to identify and address users’ suicidal ideation or expressions of self-harm.
Platforms must also disclose that interactions are artificially generated, and minors must be provided break reminders and prevented from viewing sexually explicit images generated by the chatbot.

Platforms will be required to share protocols for dealing with self-harm and statistics regarding how often they provided users with crisis center prevention notifications to the Department of Public Health.
provide families with a private right to pursue legal actions against noncompliant and negligent developers
